question_text: If xʸ + yˣ = aᵇ, show that dy/dx = −[(yx^(y−1) + yˣ log y)/(xʸ log x + xy^(x−1))].

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what the right side of the equation tells you, and what you do with the two terms on the left.
formula_note: xʸ + yˣ is a sum, so log(xʸ + yˣ) is not log(xʸ) + log(yˣ) — each term needs its own logarithm and its own product rule, then the two results are added, with aᵇ differentiating to zero since it is a constant. A sibling question with xʸ = yˣ is an equality, not a sum, so one logarithm applies to the whole line.

steps.label: Split the left side and use that the right side is constant
steps.margin_note: First mark. a and b are constants, so aᵇ is a fixed number and its derivative is zero. That is why the sum of the two derivatives equals zero.
steps.memory_tip: a and b carry no x, so aᵇ is just a number. The derivative of a number is 0, and that 0 is what the two derivatives must add up to.

steps.why: Reading aᵇ as a constant is the step that turns the problem into a single equation in dy/dx. Splitting into u and v is needed because a logarithm changes a power into a product but does nothing to a sum.
common_mistakes: Taking log of the whole left side as log(xʸ) + log(yˣ), which is log of a product, not of a sum.
Treating aᵇ as a variable and differentiating it to something other than zero.

steps.label: Differentiate the first term
steps.margin_note: Two marks. y is a function of x, so differentiating y log x needs the product rule and gives a dy/dx. Note xʸ · (1/x) = xʸ⁻¹, which is where that power in the printed answer comes from.
steps.memory_tip: xʸ divided by x is xʸ⁻¹. Reducing the power by one here is what makes the answer match the printed form.

Leaving y·xʸ/x unsimplified, so the answer never reaches the printed xʸ⁻¹.

steps.label: Add the two derivatives and collect dy/dx
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Add (2) and (3) and set the sum to zero, then take dy/dx outside a bracket. Two terms carry dy/dx and two do not, so the sort is clean.
steps.memory_tip: Sort the four terms into two groups: the terms with dy/dx and the terms without. The first group forms the bracket; the second group moves to the other side and changes sign.

steps.why: The question states the answer, so the mark is for reaching that exact arrangement: the minus outside, the two log-free and log-carrying terms in the right places, and the bracket from step (4) underneath.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign, which gives the wrong sign for the derivative.
Exchanging the numerator and the denominator, so the answer is the reciprocal.

insider_note: aᵇ is a CONSTANT, so the derivative of the whole left side is zero — that is what makes the answer a single negative fraction. Take logarithms of u and v separately, since the logarithm of a sum cannot be split.
